title: CaN: A Core-aware Neural Framework for Attributed Hypergraph Generation

problem.claim: Attributed hypergraph generation must jointly model higher-order interaction topology and dependencies between structure and node attributes.

gap.claim: Existing methods are largely topology-driven and therefore have limited ability to capture coupling among attribute semantics, structural roles, and member co-occurrence patterns.

contributions.claim: CaN is a core-aware neural generation framework for attributed hypergraphs.
CaN uses hierarchical k-core structure as an explicit generative prior and deep neural encoders for dependencies among multi-dimensional node attributes.
CaN combines core-aware structural feature allocation, dynamic autoregressive member assignment, and two-stage optimization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world attributed hypergraphs show effectiveness in structural fidelity and structure--attribute consistency.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames attributed hypergraph generation as joint modeling of topology and node attributes.
It identifies topology-driven existing methods as insufficient for modeling structural and attribute coupling.
It proposes the CaN core-aware neural generation framework.
CaN uses k-core priors, attribute encoders, constrained structural feature allocation, and autoregressive member assignment.
A two-stage optimization strategy is reported, followed by experiments assessing structural fidelity and structure--attribute consistency.

source_observation.claim: The framework introduces explicit structural priors and constraints while modeling attribute dependencies.

interpretation.claim: Generation quality may improve when structural roles and attribute semantics are modeled jointly rather than treating attributes only as auxiliary conditions.

application.claim: For attributed higher-order structure generation, consider combining structural-role priors, attribute representations, and feasibility constraints.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this design generalizes beyond the reported real-world attributed hypergraphs.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details or ablation results for the proposed modules and optimization strategy.
